what: Hershey is the largest chocolate maker in the United States. It owns Hershey's, Reese's, Kit Kat in the US, Jolly Rancher and Twizzlers, and has been buying salty snack brands such as SkinnyPop and Dot's Pretzels.
customers: American shoppers through supermarkets, convenience stores, drug stores and club retailers.
money: SkinnyPop, Dot's Pretzels and related brands
moat: Brands bought on impulse at the checkout, with shelf space and seasonal displays that a new entrant cannot buy its way into.
risks: Cocoa prices rose to record levels and crushed the gross margin
Gross margin fell to about 34%, far below its historical level
Consumers have cut back on snacks as prices rose
opportunities: A dividend yield above 3% with a long payment record
Cocoa prices have begun easing from their peaks, which would restore margin
Salty snacks diversify it away from chocolate
watch: Cocoa costs and whether gross margin recovers, plus confectionery volumes.
